content.short: JEB Decompiler is a decompiler for EVM code.
content.description: The JEB Decompiler provides code analysis to determine contract methods without access to an ABI, allowing researchers to study contracts based on compiled bytecode alone. It is widely used by security auditors, vulnerability researchers, and reverse engineers who investigate opaque smart contracts on Ethereum. Its EVM code analyzer analyzes a contract's public and private methods, including implementations of public methods synthesized by compilers, helping researchers understand potential vulnerabilities without relying on an ABI.

resources.title: Reversing Nvidia GPU SASS Code
resources.tldr: Long and deeply technical work on decompiling GPU assembly, a target with almost no tooling. Far outside the usual crypto reading and better for it.

resources.title: Deobfuscation Ratings, Inlining Fat Functions, and Breaking Opaque Predicates
resources.tldr: Concrete techniques for undoing deliberate obfuscation. Relevant to anyone trying to understand what an unverified contract or binary actually does.

resources.title: Mutation-Resistant Library Code Matching
resources.tldr: Identifying known library code even after it has been altered to avoid detection. The cat-and-mouse framing makes the problem unusually easy to follow.
